design_gotchas.title: Exposed PowerPAD IS the ONLY AGND Pin on 8-Pin DDA Package (Not Optional Heat Sink!)
design_gotchas.detail: Unlike 12-pin RNX VQFN (which has a dedicated Pin 6 AGND), the 8-pin DDA HSOIC uses its bottom exposed PowerPAD as the sole analog ground reference for internal regulator logic and feedback (Table 6-1, p.5). Failing to solder the PowerPAD solidly to ground breaks regulation and violates the ±0.3 V AGND-to-PGND abs max (p.6).

design_gotchas.title: DDA HSOIC Has Higher RDS-ON (95/66 mOhm) & Slower tON-MIN (75/108 ns) Than Page-1 RNX Headlines
design_gotchas.detail: Page 1 advertises 75/50 mOhm MOSFETs and 68 ns tON-MIN—those specs apply ONLY to the HotRod VQFN-12 (RNX) package! Per Table 7.5 & 7.6 (p.8), LMR33630ADDAR (DDA HSOIC-8) runs 95 mOhm typ (160 max) HS, 66 mOhm typ (110 max) LS, and 75 ns typ (108 ns max) tON-MIN, raising conduction loss slightly while offering much better 42.9 °C/W RθJA than RNX (72.5 °C/W).

design_gotchas.title: EN Cannot Float & Both EN/PG Must Never Exceed VIN + 0.3 V During Sequencing
design_gotchas.detail: Pin 3 (EN) has no pullup—floating EN causes indeterminate behavior (Table 6-1, p.5). Although EN can tie directly to VIN up to 36 V, Footnote 2 (p.6) prohibits pulling EN or open-drain PG above VIN + 0.3 V (for instance, from an always-on 3.3 V MCU rail while VIN is 0 V). Also never load Pin 6 (VCC, 5 V internal LDO) externally beyond a 100 kOhm PG pullup.

design_gotchas.title: Incompatible SOIC-8E Pinout vs Legacy TPS5430DDAR / TPS54331DR & 'A' (400 kHz) vs 'B'/'C' Suffixes
design_gotchas.detail: LMR33630ADDAR (1=PGND, 2=VIN, 3=EN, 4=PG, 5=FB, 6=VCC, 7=BOOT, 8=SW) cannot drop onto TPS5430DDAR or TPS54331DR pads. Also verify the frequency suffix on BOM orders: 'A' = 400 kHz (needs 6.8–8 uH inductor, marking '33630A'), 'B' = 1.4 MHz (2.2 uH), and 'C' = 2.1 MHz (1.2–1.5 uH).

typical_use_cases: 24 V industrial PLC, HVAC, motor-drive, and factory automation 3 A rails needing 3.8–36 V input, >95% efficiency, and 24 uA low-IQ light-load PFM
Modern synchronous SOIC-8E redesign replacing legacy non-synchronous TPS5430DDAR or TPS54331DR to eliminate the external Schottky diode and slash IQ 80x
High-conversion-ratio 24 V/36 V to 3.3 V/5 V step-down converters benefiting from 400 kHz ('A' suffix) low switching loss and integrated Power-Good flag
engineering_summary: The Texas Instruments LMR33630ADDAR is a rugged 3.8 V to 36 V input (38 V abs max), 3 A continuous synchronous buck converter in an 8-pin DDA HSOIC PowerPAD package (RθJA = 42.9 °C/W, RθJC(bot) = 4.3 °C/W) operating at 400 kHz ('A' suffix) with 24 uA typ PFM IQ, 1.000 V (±1.5%) VFB, precision 1.231 V EN, and an open-drain Power-Good flag. Compared with HotRod RNX VQFN-12, DDA trades slightly higher 95/66 mOhm RDS-ON and 75 ns tON-MIN for easier inspection and superior thermal resistance, while requiring its exposed PowerPAD to be soldered solidly as the sole AGND pin and keeping EN/PG <= VIN + 0.3 V.

audit_notes: 300 DPI PNG Vision on p.1 confirmed >95% peak efficiency curve at 400 kHz VOUT=5 V (~95% @ 12 V, ~96.5% @ 8 V) and 3.8–36 V / 3 A SIMPLE SWITCHER summary.
